steps: I: pastries are chocolates, cakes unconstrained for pastries, so 'no pastry is cake' not forced (fails)
II: some chocolates are cookies, all cookies are cakes, so some cakes are chocolates (holds)
check_code:
import itertools
# items: types over (pastry, choc, cookie, cake)
types=[t for t in itertools.product([0,1],repeat=4) if (not t[0] or t[1]) and (not t[2] or t[3])]
res=[]
for r in range(1,len(types)+1):
    for m in itertools.combinations(types,r):
        if any(t[1] and t[2] for t in m):
            res.append(m)
c1=all(all(not(t[0] and t[3]) for t in m) for m in res)
c2=all(any(t[3] and t[1] for t in m) for m in res)
ans={(True,True):"A",(False,False):"B",(False,True):"C",(True,False):"D"}[(c1,c2)]
assert ans=="C"
assert ans!="A" and ans!="B" and ans!="D"

steps: Synonym of Difficult among options: Complex
Trivial means easy, Imaginary and Wrong unrelated
Series is YTY repeated four times
Pos 8 = T fits; filling blanks gives TYTYYT
All red green, all green pink, no pink blue => no green is blue (I follows)
II: red are green, hence not blue; some blue are red contradicts (fails)
check_code:
import itertools
types=[t for t in itertools.product([0,1],repeat=4) if (not t[0] or t[1]) and (not t[1] or t[2]) and not(t[2] and t[3])]
# (red,green,pink,blue)
res=[m for r in range(1,len(types)+1) for m in itertools.combinations(types,r)]
c1=all(all(not(t[1] and t[3]) for t in m) for m in res)
c2=all(any(t[3] and t[0] for t in m) for m in res)
ans={(True,True):"C",(False,False):"A",(False,True):"D",(True,False):"B"}[(c1,c2)]
assert ans=="B"
assert ans!="A" and ans!="C" and ans!="D"
